question: If origin is said to come from the ṣaṇṭha letters, how can ṣaṇṭha-ness apply here?
premises: An objection arises because origin is said to come from the ṣaṇṭha letters.
This seems to imply ṣaṇṭha-ness in the present case.
The reply is that the ṣaṇṭha is not the producer here.
inference: Therefore the presence of ṣaṇṭha letters does not make the ṣaṇṭha the generative principle in this context.
uncertainties: The technical term ṣaṇṭha is retained in transliteration because its doctrinal meaning is specific.
plain_english: An objection is raised: if origin is said to come from the ṣaṇṭha letters, how can ṣaṇṭha-ness apply here? The answer is that in this case the ṣaṇṭha is not the producer.
